title: How long light takes to reach us from the Moon and Sun
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: How long does sunlight take to reach Earth?
If the Sun went out, how long before we noticed?

explain.say: Light is the fastest thing there is, travelling about 300 thousand kilometres every second. It could zip around the Earth about seven times in one second.

draw.text: How long light takes to reach us from the Moon and Sun

explain.say: The Moon is about 384 thousand kilometres away, so moonlight takes about 1.3 seconds to reach your eyes.
The Sun is about 150 million kilometres away, so sunlight takes about 8 minutes and 20 seconds to arrive. You always see the Sun as it was eight minutes ago.
Starlight takes far longer: years, centuries or more. So when you look at the night sky, you are looking back in time.

faq.a: Light travels at about 300 thousand kilometres per second in empty space, or nearly 300 million metres every second. Nothing travels faster.
asks: What is the speed of light?

faq.q: How long does sunlight take to reach Earth?
faq.a: On average about 8 minutes and 20 seconds, because the Sun is about 150 million kilometres away. So we see the Sun as it was a few minutes ago.
asks: How far is the Sun in light minutes?

faq.q: If the Sun went out, how long before we noticed?
faq.a: We would keep seeing it for about 8 minutes and 20 seconds, because the last light it gave out would still be on its way to us.
asks: Would we see the Sun vanish straight away?

faq.a: A light-year is the distance light travels in one year, about 9.5 million million kilometres. It measures distance, not time.

faq.q: How long does light from the nearest star take?
faq.a: The nearest star beyond the Sun, Proxima Centauri, is about 4.2 light-years away. Its light left it more than four years before it reaches your eyes.
asks: Are we seeing stars in the past?

facts: Light travels at 299,792 kilometres per second in a vacuum.
Sunlight takes on average about 8 minutes 20 seconds (about 499 seconds) to reach Earth.
Moonlight takes about 1.3 seconds to reach Earth.

quiz.say: If the Sun suddenly went dark, about how long would it be before we saw it go out?
quiz.show: We would see the Sun go dark after about…
quiz.why: Sunlight takes about 8 minutes 20 seconds to cross the 150 million kilometres to Earth.

wrong.0: Light is fast but not instant; the Sun's last light would still be travelling.
wrong.2: Light is much faster than that; 8 days of travel would put the Sun far beyond Neptune.
